world-bible.json.name: Godbones

voice.style: Pratchett-style: warm, dry, omniscient narrator who knows exactly how absurd everyone is and likes them anyway. Long sentences that wander and then land a punchline in the last four words. Grand mythic statements immediately undercut by small domestic detail. Wry asides that state the obvious nobody wanted said. Plain, concrete diction, no purple prose. Humor carries the darkness instead of hiding it.
sample_passages: Three hundred years ago the god Aldrumm fell out of the sky, which is the sort of thing that happens to gods eventually, and landed across the Weeping Valley like a dropped coat. The people of the valley did what people always do with a disaster: they waited a respectful week, then moved in.
The Chapel of the Long Wake held that Aldrumm was merely sleeping. This was a comfort to the faithful and a considerable relief to the Chapel's accountants, since nobody tithes to a corpse.

Magic, old Mother Gristle told her apprentices, is very simple. You say the true name of a thing in the god's own tongue, and the thing listens. Then it sends you the bill. Most people who die of magic, she added, die of not reading the bill.

world-bible.json.tone: Dark with humor. Death, debt, and divine murder are real and lethal; the people living through them are petty, funny, stubborn, and kind at inconvenient moments.
themes: living off the dead: a whole town that eats, burns, and sells pieces of its god
inheritance and lineage: who gets to own a god's body, and who did the actual hauling
faith as a business: the Chapel needs Aldrumm asleep, not dead and not awake
the price of power: every word of magic is paid for in the caster's own body
an unfinished murder: the goddess who killed Aldrumm has not stopped working

nodes.name: The Wardens of the Sternum
nodes.summary: Council of the old Bearer families whose ancestors hauled the god's body. Hold hereditary rights to the bones and collect the marrow tithe. Pompous, inbred, genuinely brave when cornered.

nodes.name: The Chapel of the Long Wake
nodes.summary: Insists Aldrumm is only sleeping. Sells dream-blessings, keeps the Heartstone, and quietly bans the Marrowtongue as blasphemy (and competition).

nodes.name: The Marrow Guild
nodes.summary: Tithe-scrapers and pit-crews who mine glowing marrow from the bones for lamps, medicine, and magic. Working people with sore backs and long memories.

nodes.name: The Lantern Tutors
nodes.summary: The handful of licensed teachers of the Marrowtongue. Scarce, expensive, and each one a little odd from years of paying the Toll.

nodes.name: The Hollow Choir
nodes.summary: Servants of the Carrion Queen, the goddess who killed Aldrumm. They want his heart, and they are patient, polite, and already in town.

edges.relation: tithe dispute; the Guild does the digging, the Wardens take the cut
condemns as blasphemers, yet secretly hires them
has infiltrated; wants the Heartstone it guards

nodes.name: Rib Row
nodes.summary: The starting street: a market lane built along the inside curve of the seventh rib. Shops are carved into the bone; the street slopes, so everything rolls downhill eventually, including reputations.

nodes.name: The Marrow Pits
nodes.summary: Bore-holes into the great rib bones where the Guild scrapes glowing marrow. Warm, humming, and occasionally dreaming.

nodes.name: The Chapel of the Long Wake
nodes.summary: Built over the god's still heart-cavity at the center of the Ribcage.

nodes.name: The Spine Road
nodes.summary: The old road running along the god's backbone out of the Ribcage toward the north.

nodes.name: The Skull
nodes.summary: A sealed hill of bone a day north. Nobody goes in. People who say they have are lying or changed.

nodes.name: The Open Hand
nodes.summary: Five finger-bones jutting out of farmland to the east; a rival village lives in the palm.

nodes.name: Pelvis Fen
nodes.summary: Marshland south of the hips. Bad smells, worse neighbors.

edges.adjacency: down a stair cut into the rib
a short climb toward the sternum
the Spine Road starts behind the Chapel
a day's walk north along the vertebrae

timeline: The Last Quarrel: the gods fight; the Carrion Queen kills Aldrumm the Hearthfather
The Fall: Aldrumm lands across the Weeping Valley
The Bearing: twelve families drag the body into position and claim it (roughly 300 years ago)
The town of Godbones is built inside the ribcage; the Chapel of the Long Wake is founded
Now: marrow yields are dropping, dreams are shared across town, and the Hollow Choir has arrived

pantheon.name: Aldrumm the Hearthfather
pantheon.note: The dead (sleeping?) god of hearth, harvest, and keeping promises. His bones are the town.

pantheon.name: The Carrion Queen
pantheon.note: Goddess of endings and scavengers. Killed Aldrumm in the Last Quarrel and wants to finish eating.

pantheon.name: Old Tamsin of the Crossroads
pantheon.note: Trickster goddess who sat the Quarrel out. Still sells advice at bad prices.

signature_systems: Marrowtongue magic: speak a thing's true name in the dead god's language and it obeys. Infinitely flexible, but every working is paid from the caster's own body (the Toll). Bigger ambition, bigger bill. Untutored casters pay extra.
The Toll: a price roll after every working; ranges from a headache to collapse to death.
The Stirring: a town-wide meter of how close Aldrumm is to waking. Big magic near the bones and desecration push it up. Thresholds bring shared dreams, bone-quakes, and finally an opened eye.
Bearer Standing: NPC reactions are shifted by your lineage and reputation with the old families.

npcs.name: Mother Gristle
npcs.note: Ancient Lantern Tutor of the Marrowtongue who runs a pickle shop on Rib Row as cover and takes one apprentice a decade.

npcs.name: Warden Osric Hallowmere
npcs.note: Head of the senior Bearer family; pompous, broke, and desperate to keep the tithe flowing.

npcs.name: Deacon Ilsabet Vane
npcs.note: Rising star of the Chapel of the Long Wake, very warm, very helpful, secretly of the Hollow Choir.

npcs.name: Brannoc Tull
npcs.note: Foreman of the Marrow Guild, built like a door, organizing a strike nobody is supposed to call a strike.

npcs.name: Pip Haddersley
npcs.note: Street urchin and marrow-thief who has been having the god's dreams every night.

npcs.name: Brother Pellam Smudge
npcs.note: The Chapel's underpaid illuminator, who paints everything that happens and gets most of it slightly wrong.

locations.name: Rib Row
locations.note: The market lane along the seventh rib; the opening stage.

locations.name: Gristle's Pickles & Preserves
locations.note: Mother Gristle's shop; the back room is a schoolroom for dangerous words.

locations.name: The Marrow Pits
locations.note: Guild mines bored into the ribs.

locations.name: The Chapel of the Long Wake
locations.note: Built over the heart-cavity; holds the Heartstone.

locations.name: The Skull
locations.note: Sealed bone hill a day north; forbidden.

items.name: The Heartstone
items.note: Crystallized last heartbeat of Aldrumm, kept by the Chapel; the Hollow Choir wants it.

items.name: Marrow lamp
items.note: Common lantern burning refined god-marrow; warm amber light, faint humming.

items.name: Bearer's Ring
items.note: Bone signet proving descent from one of the twelve hauling families.

monsters.name: Marrow-mites
monsters.note: Dog-sized pale insects that burrow in the bones and eat marrow, and occasionally miners.

monsters.name: The Hollow-sung
monsters.note: People the Choir has emptied out and filled with the Carrion Queen's hymn; polite, tireless, wrong.

monsters.name: Bone-wight
monsters.note: A Bearer ancestor's ghost bound into a rib; furious about property lines.
